aliases: Compass Data Centers Stamey Farm Road
status_detail: Statesville City Council agenda listed rezoning request ZC25-13 for Compass Data Centers on Stamey Farm Road between I-40 and US 70; local/TNS coverage reported City Council unanimously approved the planned data center on about 330 acres on Sept. 15, 2025. Reported scope: five 270,000-square-foot buildings, about 200 jobs, closed-loop hybrid cooling, and backup generators.
notes: Project name spelling appears as both Statesville and 'Stateville' in trackers; official/local materials use Statesville.

status_detail: Tract proposed a data center campus on roughly 399-400 acres owned by Earnhardt Farms/Teresa Earnhardt near Patterson Farm Road and Coddle Creek. DCD reported up to five buildings, 1.5 million square feet, possible 2028 construction start, 2029 initial power, and up to $30B over 20 years. WSOC reported in August 2025 that Mooresville commissioners were set to deny the rezoning; later search snippets indicate plans were withdrawn/scrapped after opposition.
notes: Final disposition is based on local-news/search evidence of denial posture and withdrawal/scrapping; official agenda archive was checked but exact final action page was not isolated during the quick pass.

aliases: Helix Ventures and PointOne technology park
developer: PointOne Data Centers / Helix Ventures; CyrusOne as owner/operator/end user
status_detail: PointOne and CyrusOne describe a proposed multiphase Lee County campus near Sanford at 4079 Lower Moncure Road. PointOne lists a 430-acre full site and Phase One as one data center building totaling 90 MW IT load for CyrusOne. SAGA reported a $900M Phase One built-infrastructure investment, no local incentives, local utility power, and expected construction later in 2026 with first customers in early 2028 if permitted. Local planning/news describe the TRC application as a 428.85-acre light-industrial data center with fire-water tank, pump house, public water/sewer, and building-permit submittal as the next step after preliminary review.
notes: CyrusOne states the project is not fracking, onsite fuel extraction, or cryptocurrency mining and would operate under Lee County data center standards.
